title: Microcanary Stewardship Checklist — Live Trial Sandbox
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working sandbox checklist for running very small, heavily stewarded canaries ("microcanaries") and A/B trials for LLM-driven features in the Console. Focus: cross-functional ops -> minimize blast radius while getting realistic signal on behavior, cost, and safety. Intended audience: rollout steward (owner), SRE on-call, Product PM, Safety reviewer, Solutions eng for customer-facing trials.

Notes to self (why microcanary):
- We need earlier detection of quality regressions (hallucination, refusal drops) that unit tests and offline evals miss.
- Microcanary = <1% traffic or targeted cohort (internal beta users), synthetic + real traffic mixing, heavy human-in-loop sampling.
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive about telemetry windows, gating thresholds, communications cadence.

Before activation (pre-flight): quick checklist
- Owner assigned and on-call rota updated (steward: @Maya Li).
- Create experiment: name and hypothesis in Console and link to INF Jira (INF-7890).
- Confirm model variant compatibility: fallback variants defined (e.g., gpt-large-v1 -> gpt-large-quant-v1).
- Confirm config pin: max tokens, stop sequences, function-calling schema.
- Prepare synthetic traffic generator (lab-run ID) and smoke test script.
- Cost guardrails: set per-minute token budget and burst throttle. Budget example: daily token cap for trial = 200k tokens.
- Ops checklist: enable tracing hooks (request_id -> trace), ensure prefix cache warming scheduled.
- Safety review: short safety note + acceptance criteria in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-3421).

Cohort design and exposure plan
- Phase 0: internal dogfood only (10–20 engineers). Duration: 24–72h. Purpose: catch obvious errors and infra regressions.
- Phase 1: microcanary to low-risk production cohort (<0.5% of traffic OR 200 users), mixing 30% synthetic queries to exercise edge patterns. Duration: 3–7 days.
- Phase 2: broaden to 2–5% with automatic monitoring and weekly manual review.
- A/B split design: when applicable, run 50/50 within cohort for quality metrics (A=control, B=variant). For cost/latency measurement might prefer deterministic routing to avoid cross-contamination.

Key metrics to collect (primary signals):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99; target p95 < 450ms for interactive routes.
- Error rate: 5xx and model failures; alert at >0.5% over 30m.
- Token cost delta: per-request token cost delta vs control; abort if +15% sustained over 6h.
- Safety scoring: automated safety classifier rate and human-review harm-rate. Gate if classifier-detected harm delta > 0.02 (2 percentage points) or human escalation shows any critical harm.
- Semantic quality: upstream eval harness (prompt-set agreement score) — require no regression > 1.5% on critical prompts.
- Behavioral regressions: hallucination flag rate, refusal-drop rate.
- Customer-facing signals: CTR change, downstream conversion, support queue volume.

Telemetry windows and sweep cadence
- Real-time sweep (every 5m): latency, 5xx, request volume, token burn. Auto alerting for severity tiers.
- Signal sweep (hourly): safety classifier delta, token cost trend, sample counts for human review.
- Cohort sweep (daily): semantic-quality aggregate, customer metric deltas.
- Manual human review: sample 50 outputs/day for the first 3 days, then 25/day for the next week. Focus on edge prompts.

Gating thresholds (example values, conservative):
- Immediate abort (automatic revert): 5xx spike > 1% sustained 15m OR latency p99 > 2s for 10m.
- High-severity manual rollback: safety classifier delta > 5% OR any verified harmful output to a paying customer.
- Slow-fail auto-rollback: sustained token cost increase > 20% over 24h.
- Soft-warning: semantic-quality drop 1.5–3% (requires joint PM + Safety review).

Human-in-the-loop flows and sampling
- Sampling policy: stratified by user type and prompt length. Bias towards long contexts and function-calling.
- Channel for human review: reviewers submit findings to rollouts/responses spreadsheet and tag with severity L1/L2/L3.
- Escalation: L3 -> immediate paging of steward + SRE; L2 -> Slack notification and 1-hour steering sync; L1 -> triage in daily sweep.

Rollback and remediation playbook
- Step 0: steward triggers rollback from Console -> route 100% back to control variant.
- Step 1: open Rollback Incident (template linked) and set severity. Add linked artifacts (Jira INF-7890).
- Step 2: collect artifact bundle (traces, request samples, config snapshot, model binary tag).
- Step 3: if safety-related, run immediate offline replay on safety harness and quarantine affected prompts.
- Step 4: mitigation: toggle token-throttle, reduce max-response-length, or switch to higher-safety variant.
- Post-incident: 48h retrospective + 5-whys + action items assigned.

Experiment power and sample notes (back-of-envelope)
- For quality metric that moves ~2 percentage points, to get ~80% power at alpha 0.05 in an A/B test, we need ~10k samples per arm (depends on baseline variance). For microcanaries, we accept low power but high signal fidelity with human sampling.

Cross-functional responsibilities (roles)
- Steward (Product): overall owner for go/no-go decisions, coordinates reviews, ensures comms.
- SRE / On-call: infra monitoring, rollback, tracing.
- Safety reviewer: clears safety gates, leads human review.
- Solutions/SE: customer-specific behavior, config tuning, on-call for customer trial.
- Data & Observability: ensures dashboards and sample pipelines are live.

Communications plan
- Pre-activation: one-pager + 1-h sync with stakeholders (SRE, Safety, Support, Eng).
- On activation: Slack: #rollouts notify channel, pager duty runbook contact.
- Daily: morning status in channel for first week.
- Post-rollback: summary + action items in Confluence and brief for Exec if customer-impacting.

Operational nitty-gritty (small notes)
- Prefix caching: pre-warm top 50 prompt prefixes mapped to cohort.
- KV cache considerations: warn on large kv entries; include kv eviction policy in config snapshot.
- Feature flags: prefer flags that can flip per-route, not global, to avoid mass exposure.
- Synthetic traffic: annotate synthetic queries as such to avoid contaminating A/B signals.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide safe sample size for human review after day 3. Rough proposal: 25/day.
- Formalize severity taxonomy for output harms and add to telemetry event schema.
- Run a tabletop for rollback scripts with SRE.

Quick links and artifacts
- Runbook template: CONFLUENCE-3421
- Jira: INF-7890 (experiment tracker), PS-234 (postmortem template)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/412

Scratch notes (things to try later):
- Canary-by-intent: route only queries with intent tag "editorial" to variant to reduce exposure to sensitive intents.
- Adaptive sampling: increase human review sampling when classifier confidence < 0.6.
- Cost-aware bucket: throttle variant when token burn hits 80% of trial budget.

End of sandbox checklist.
This is intentionally terse and iterative — use as working reference and annotate with real signals during a live experiment.
